text: Writing clean code is a skill that helps both you and your team. The most important goal is to make your code readable. Use clear naming conventions for variables, functions, and classes; for example, `calculateTotalPrice` is much better than `ctp`. Break your code into small, focused functions, each doing only one thing. This approach makes your code easier to test and reuse. When your functions are simple, you reduce complexity and improve maintainability. Remember, clean code means someone else—or even you in six months—can understand and modify it without frustration. It is not just about working code; it is about code that works well for people.
